A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and retain matching core experiments and equations. All 18 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including their figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on three QA datasets, including faithfulness measurements, inference-time sampling, Logit Lens analyses, causal mediation and judge validation.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds larger-model and reasoning-model experiments, another judge comparison, and qualitative CoT examples.

M1.justification: The hint-injection procedure, faithfulness metrics, faithful@k estimator, unlearning procedure, Logit Lens method and causal interventions remain unchanged. Additional model configurations and sampling evaluations do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ARC-Easy, OpenbookQA and StrategyQA using Professor, Metadata and Black Squares hints. The added models use subsets of this existing coverage; no new dataset, task or input scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds an actual comparison with a GPT-4o judge on the same 100 human-annotated examples previously used to assess gpt-oss-20b. The principal comparison among Biasing Features, Filler Tokens and FUR is retained.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds a 4-bit Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct configuration and Qwen-3-32B in thinking mode on two retained datasets. Section 5.2 extends faithful@k from k up to 16 to k up to 32; retaining the n >= max(k) rule raises the reported eligibility threshold. These are substantive evaluation-setting additions and revisions.

E4.justification: v2 extends mechanism analyses and the strict lexical non-verbalization robustness check to larger and reasoning models, adds the GPT-4o judge crosscheck, and introduces four paired CoT case studies in Appendix E. The original smaller-model judge-error robustness analysis was already present in v1 and is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use 95% bootstrap intervals, including 10,000-resample BCa intervals for causal mediation. Added results retain these reporting practices; no change to seed reporting, repeated-run counts or uncertainty-estimation procedures is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the two additional models, k = 32, judge validation and qualitative examples. For example, Table 2 reports 47/65 Qwen-3-32B CoTs as faithful under Filler Tokens on OpenbookQA with Black Squares hints. Appendix D adds GPT-4o's 87% accuracy and 80% precision. The original five tables' numerical bodies are retained within their corresponding v2 tables.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same metric definitions, faithful@k estimator, activation decoding, mediation effects and unlearning controls. The new causal diagram illustrates existing mathematics; no new formal assumptions, theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The three central findings and headline thresholds remain. v2 extends the stated empirical applicability to larger and reasoning models and explicitly qualifies the abstract: it does not claim all CoTs are faithful, only that missing hint words alone do not establish unfaithfulness.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands discussion of faithful@k's inability to distinguish occasional faithfulness from incomplete verbalization at the instance level, and incompleteness from non-exhaustiveness. It also introduces sycophancy as an explanation for Professor-hint behavior and interprets Qwen's negative Metadata indirect effects as suppression. The judge-error caveat itself already existed in v1's appendix.

D1.justification: The code disclosure changes from a promised future release to stated availability with a repository link. v2 also supplies the quantized Llama checkpoint reference and sampling parameters for the additional models. Existing implementation libraries, hardware descriptions and judge instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Arcuschin et al. (2025) and Paul et al. (2024), distinguishing its mediation setup from the latter. Related Work more explicitly acknowledges prior support for CoT monitoring and causal verification, positioning the paper as complementary while retaining its critique of hint-based evaluation.

P1.justification: v2 revises portions of the abstract, introduction, metric explanations and results discussion, adds Related Work subheadings, and renames the concluding section Discussion. It inserts a generalization section and swaps Appendices A/B, while retaining the main methodological sequence and much of the exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds a causal graph, larger-model diagnostic plots and a paired-CoT example table, and expands existing result tables and plot panels. It rearranges faithful@k displays and standardizes plot colors and terminology. Figures 3–4 also correct the vertical-axis label from Unfaithfulness to Faithfulness.

improvement.justification: The new larger-model and reasoning-model experiments directly address v1's explicit limitation of supporting broad conclusions using only small instruction-tuned models. Additional judge validation, qualitative examples and clearer qualifications strengthen scrutiny and applicability. The new monotonicity argument does not resolve faithful@k's ambiguity about occasional faithfulness, but the expanded relevant evidence and clearer boundaries provide a substantial net improvement.
